headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 3 studies yielded an effect size of 1.02 (95% CI: 0.73–1.41), indicating no statistically significant association between lycopene and renal cell carcinoma. Although the point estimate suggests a potential positive relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by substantial heterogeneity (I² = 74.19%), reflecting considerable variability across studies.

effect_size.excerpt: Compared with <100 g/d, the pooled multivariate RRs (95% CI) for >or=400 g/d were 0.79 (0.63-0.99; P for trend = 0.03) for total fruit and 0.72 (0.48-1.08; P for trend = 0.07) for total vegetables. sample_size.location: PATIENTS AND METHODS / Study population, paragraph 2; total_n derived from reported group counts 1142 + 1154 = 2296

cases.excerpt: Sociodemographic and baseline health characteristics and nutrient intake levels of 1142 cases and 1154 controls in the eligible study population are presented by race in Table 1 . Compared to controls, cases were more likely to report a lower education level, smoke, have a higher BMI and family history of RCC, and diagnosed with hypertension.
cases.location: PATIENTS AND METHODS / Study population, paragraph 2

comparison.excerpt: Daily micronutrient intake (mg/day) was categorized into quartiles based on control distributions; the three lower quartiles were each compared to the highest quartile.
comparison.location: PATIENTS AND METHODS / Statistical analysis, paragraph 1

design.excerpt: The US Kidney Cancer Study is a population‐based case‐control study designed to examine racial disparities between AA and EA in RCC risk.
design.location: PATIENTS AND METHODS / Study population, paragraph 1

timing.excerpt: enrolled in a population‐based case‐control study between 2002 and 2007. Dietary micronutrient intake was derived from an interviewer‐administered diet history questionnaire.

continent.excerpt: The study was conducted in the metropolitan areas of Detroit (Wayne, Oakland, and Macomb counties), Michigan and Chicago (Cook County), Illinois.
continent.location: PATIENTS AND METHODS / Study population, paragraph 1

ethnicity.excerpt: 1142 EA and AA RCC cases and 1154 frequency‐matched controls were enrolled in a population‐based case‐control study

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Dietary micronutrient intake was derived from an interviewer-administered diet history questionnaire.
exposure_measurement.location: PATIENTS AND METHODS / Data collection, paragraph 2

gender.excerpt: Controls were frequency matched to cases 2:1 in AA and 1:1 in EA on study center, race, sex, and five‐year age categories.
gender.location: PATIENTS AND METHODS / Study population, paragraph 1

smoking_status.excerpt: Adjusted models included variables for: region (Detroit, Chicago), sex (male, female), race (White, African American), age (20‐44, 45‐54, 55‐64, 65‐74, 75+), education (<12 years, high school graduate, some college, 4+ years of college), smoking history (never, occasional/unknown, former, current)
smoking_status.location: PATIENTS AND METHODS / Statistical analysis, paragraph 3
